RESULT: obsctl analyze now gates remote endpoints on a new knob analyze.remote_consent (bool, default false, observe.json + registry card): remote and false prints a consent line (event count, host, model, knob, secrets-redacted note), sends nothing and exits 1 with OBS_FAIL; remote and true prints the same line before sending; local endpoints never need it. Every serialized event passes through _redact_secrets (checkctl.SECRET_PATTERNS imported, matches become [REDACTED:<name>]) before truncation and before the request is built, local and remote. analyze_status() carries remote_consent and consent_required booleans (the console payload passes them through), and --dry-run reports the consent state while still sending nothing.

DEVIATIONS: consent_required is defined as 'the endpoint is remote' (bool(base_url) and not local), mirroring key_required, not as 'the gate would block'; the gate blocks when consent_required and not remote_consent. With no base_url it is false (nothing to consent to).
Only JSON true counts as consent (acfg.get('remote_consent') is True): a truthy string such as "yes" does not open the gate; pinned by test_consent_must_be_a_real_boolean.
The consent gate sits after the 'not configured' and 'no events' no-ops, so those still exit 0 and the line's event count is the real count to be sent.
The knob is documented in the observe.json analyze _comment, not in reference/secrets.md (the plan allowed either; secrets.md is not in T16's Owns list).
UNCERTAINTIES: Not run on Ubuntu (CI only); tests use no OS-specific paths and fake the remote by base_url text with _http_post_json patched.

The private_key pattern matches only the BEGIN header, so a PEM body in an event is still sent with only its header redacted: the redactor is exactly as strong as checkctl.SECRET_PATTERNS. GENERIC_QUOTED/GENERIC_BARE are not applied (the task names SECRET_PATTERNS only).

The existing local rule is a substring test ('localhost' or '127.0.0.1' anywhere in base_url), so a host like localhost.example.com counts as local and skips the consent gate; kept as the task specified.
